clues: This hill town in India sits between the Brahmaputra and Surma valleys. Green hills roll all round it.
Its air is much cooler than the air in the hot tropics of India. That cool feel was one big reason the British chose this hill town.
In 1874, the British picked this hill town as the head town for their new rule in Assam.
The green hills round this town made the British think of Scotland far away. So they gave it the name Scotland of the East.
This town is now the capital town of Meghalaya. It took that job in 1972, when that new state was born.
